title: Noticing when something is tricky
keyIdea: Noticing when a job is tricky is a learning skill. Clues tell you: a cross or worried face, the same mistake again, wanting to throw it, not knowing what to do. Tricky does not mean you are bad at it. Say it out loud ('This is tricky', 'I'm stuck'), then choose what to do: slow down, try a new way, or ask for help when you are still stuck or it is not safe.

kid: Some jobs are easy. Some jobs are tricky. Your body tells you. You may feel cross. Your face may frown. You may want to throw it.
Tricky does not mean you are bad at it. It means you are learning. Say it out loud: this is tricky. Or: I'm stuck.
Then pick what to do. Slow down. Look close. Go one bit at a time. Did the same way not work? Try a new way. Turn it. Flip it. Start at a new end.
Still stuck? Is it high up, or not safe? Ask a grown-up. Say: can you help me, please? That is smart. It is not giving up.
adult: This is an early metacognition skill: monitoring. Children notice that a task is hard, name it, and pick a strategy. In England it sits under the EYFS Characteristics of Effective Learning (active learning: keeping on trying when they meet difficulties; creating and thinking critically: changing strategy as needed). It also feeds the Early Learning Goals for Self-Regulation and Managing Self.

Key terms: monitoring means checking how a task is going while you do it. Self-regulation is managing feelings and actions to reach a goal. A strategy is a way of tackling a task, such as slowing down, trying a new way or asking. Help-seeking is asking for support once you have tried. The EEF guidance on metacognition says adults should model this thinking aloud.

Common mistakes: children often read tricky as I am bad at this, so praise the noticing (you spotted that this is tricky) rather than calling them clever. Another slip is to repeat the same move harder, such as pushing a puzzle piece again, so prompt them to change one thing. Be careful not to rescue straight away; wait a moment, then offer a choice. But for safety, such as high shelves or hot things, asking at once is right.

In the lab your child taps the signs that a job is tricky, drags the right words to Kit, steers a bee slowly along a twisty path (rushing makes it bump), turns a block that will not fit instead of pushing it again, and sorts jobs into try again or ask a grown-up.

familyTip: Think aloud when you get stuck: 'Hmm, this is tricky. I'll slow down.' Then when your child frowns at a puzzle, ask: 'Is it tricky? What could you try: slow down, a new way, or ask me?'

visual.caption: Tricky sign or going well? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap tricky signs, give Kit the words, slow a bee down on a twisty path, turn a block to try a new way, and sort try again or ask a grown-up.

practice.prompt: Noticing when something is tricky: Mo's tower falls down again and again. Mo feels cross. What is true?
choices: The job is tricky for Mo
practice.hint: A cross feeling and the same thing going wrong are clues. What do they tell Mo about the job?
practice.explain: Falling again and feeling cross are tricky signs. Tricky means Mo is still learning, not that Mo is bad at it.

practice.prompt: Kit pushed the block the same way {n} times and it bumped each time. Then Kit turned it and it went in. How many tries did Kit have in all?
practice.hint: Count the pushes that bumped, then add the one try after turning it.
practice.explain: {n} tries the same way, then 1 new way, makes {=n+1} tries. Only the new way worked.

practice.prompt: The path for the toy car is very twisty. What helps most?
choices: Go as fast as you can
practice.hint: On the bendy bits, does rushing help you stay on the path?
practice.explain: Slowing down and looking helps you steer round the bends. Rushing makes you bump.

practice.prompt: Ada has {a} jobs she can try again and {b} jobs where she needs a grown-up. How many jobs is that?
practice.hint: Put the two groups together and count them all.
practice.explain: {a} try-again jobs and {b} ask-a-grown-up jobs make {=a+b} jobs. Sorting them helps Ada choose what to do.

pool.prompt: Which one is a sign that a job is tricky?
pool.hint: Which one shows that something keeps going wrong?
pool.explain: The same mistake again is a tricky sign. The other two show the job is going well.

pool.prompt: You are stuck on a puzzle. What is a good thing to say?
pool.hint: Pick the words that tell how the job feels, not that you are bad.
pool.explain: Saying this is tricky names the problem. Then you, or a grown-up, can choose what to do.

pool.prompt: The puzzle piece bumped 2 times. What should you do next?
choices: Turn it and try a new way
Push it the same way, harder
pool.hint: If the same way keeps bumping, what can you change?
pool.explain: Doing the same thing again gets the same bump. Turning it is a new way, and it may fit.

pool.prompt: Your teddy is on a high shelf. What do you do?
pool.hint: Is climbing up high safe? Who can reach it safely?
pool.explain: High up is not safe to climb. Asking a grown-up is the smart choice here, straight away.

pool.prompt: A twisty path has {n} bends. You slow down at every bend. How many times do you slow down?
pool.hint: You slow down one time at each bend. Count the bends.
pool.explain: There are {n} bends and you slow down once at each, so you slow down {=n} times.

pool.prompt: Kit tried the zip {n} times and it was still stuck. Then Kit asked Mum and she helped once. How many goes was that?
pool.hint: Count Kit's tries, then add the one time Mum helped.
pool.explain: {n} tries by Kit and 1 with Mum make {=n+1} goes. Asking after trying is smart, not giving up.

pool.prompt: Asking for help when you are still stuck is…
pool.hint: Think about what happens next once someone helps you.
pool.explain: Asking for help after trying is a smart choice. You keep learning, and next time you may do it alone.

pool.prompt: Your drawing went wobbly because you rushed. What can you try?
choices: Slow down and have another go
Ask a grown-up to do it all
pool.hint: What made it go wobbly? What is the opposite of rushing?
pool.explain: Rushing made it wobbly, so slowing down is the fix. You can do this one yourself.
